text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A group of parliamentarians want election law amended to have one constituency instead of 25.
- Some 280 real estate purchase contracts worth $20 million were signed during a property fair in Kuwait this week.
- Trade and Industry Minister Jassem al-Mudaf, head of Arab-British chamber of commerce, discuss boosting cooperation between British and Kuwaiti firms.
- Jordanians who suffered losses due to the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Kuwait to receive compensations within a few days.
- Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates in favour of postponing the economy summit for the Middle East and North Africa scheduled in November in Qatar, Gulf diplomatic sources say.
- Parliamentary panel seeks reduction in family visa salary cap. Expatriate residents wishing to bring their families to live with them have to prove earning a minimum of 600 dinars ($2,000).
- Government seeks harsher penalties against illegal entrants.
- MP seeks information on possible gun deal with China.
- Wealthy Kuwaiti businessman commits suicide on Wednesday to avoid arrest for issuing a bad cheque for one million dinars.
